airQuality.description: Cache current AQI and hourly pollutant forecasts for one location.

steps.step1: Enter the location coordinates and timezone.
steps.step3: Confirm endpoint policy, preview, then save.

airQuality.tip: Hosted Open-Meteo access requires noncommercial acknowledgement; commercial deployments use a self-hosted endpoint.

atom.description: Turn an Atom feed into reusable records without making editors work through every technical option first.

steps.step1: Name the connection and paste the Atom feed URL.
steps.step2: Choose the fields, item limit, and sort order.
steps.step3: Preview the mapped entries, then save.

atom.tip: Use the direct Atom XML URL rather than the website homepage.

calendar.description: Connect one or more public ICS calendars, choose which event details to expose, then preview real events before saving.

steps.step1: Name the connection and paste the public ICS URL.
steps.step2: Choose the event window, fields, and timezone.
steps.step3: Preview real events, then save the Data Source.

calendar.tip: Use the public or secret iCalendar subscription URL, not the normal calendar webpage.

capAlerts.description: Normalize active public CAP 1.2 warnings from direct XML or a feed index.

steps.step1: Enter the CAP document or index URL.
steps.step2: Choose language, severity, and area filters.

capAlerts.tip: Area filters match the alert’s published area description.

csv.description: Upload a CSV or connect a hosted CSV, map its columns, and preview the rows Tilecast will cache.

steps.step1: Upload a CSV file or paste a direct CSV URL.
steps.step2: Map the column names and choose displayed fields.
steps.step3: Preview the mapped rows, then save.

csv.tip: Column names must match the first row of the CSV. Start with the title column; the others are optional.

json.description: Connect a public JSON endpoint, map its record paths, and verify the normalized result before saving.

steps.step1: Paste the public JSON endpoint URL.
steps.step2: Map the list path and the fields your Widgets need.
steps.step3: Preview the mapped records, then save.

json.tip: JSON Pointer paths begin with a slash. Use / for a top-level array or /items for { "items": [...] }.

manual.description: Create a small typed table for announcements, prices, metrics, directories, and other reusable signage data.

steps.step1: Define the typed columns your Widgets need.
steps.step2: Enter up to 200 rows directly in Studio.
steps.step3: Save and reuse the table across multiple Widgets.

manual.tip: Choose stable field keys because Widgets refer to them when selecting content.

rss.description: Turn an RSS feed into clean, cached records for lists, tickers, tables, and layouts.

steps.step1: Name the connection and paste the RSS feed URL.
steps.step2: Choose the fields, item limit, and sort order.
steps.step3: Preview the mapped posts, then save.

rss.tip: Paste the direct feed URL. It often ends in /feed, .xml, or .rss.

transit.description: Join public GTFS schedules with realtime trip updates and optional service alerts.

steps.step1: Enter the Static and Realtime feed URLs.
steps.step2: Choose stop IDs, route filters, and timezone.
steps.step3: Preview departures and alerts, then save.

transit.tip: Use stable stop IDs from the agency’s GTFS Static feed.

weather.description: Cache current conditions and a seven-day forecast for one coordinate using MET Norway.

steps.step1: Enter the location label, coordinates, and timezone.
steps.step2: Choose units and provide the required contact identity.
steps.step3: Preview the normalized forecast, then save.

weather.tip: Use coordinates rounded to four decimals and the IANA timezone for the location.
